questions.question: A dropdown inside a card with `overflow: hidden` gets clipped. Why does converting it to a `popover` fix this?
options: Popovers render in the top layer, above all stacking contexts and unclipped by ancestors' overflow
Popovers are moved to the end of the body element in the DOM
Popovers disable overflow on all ancestors
questions.explanation: The top layer sits above the normal document painting order, so z-index, stacking contexts and ancestor overflow clipping no longer apply. The element stays where it is in the DOM.

questions.question: Which popover type should a toast notification that must stay visible until you close it use?
questions.explanation: manual popovers have no light dismiss and do not close other popovers, so they stay open until code or a button hides them.

questions.question: What is the key behavioural difference between a popover and a `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()`?
options: The modal dialog makes the rest of the page inert and contains focus; a popover is non-modal
Only dialogs render in the top layer
Popovers cannot be closed with Escape
questions.explanation: Both use the top layer and support ::backdrop, but only the modal dialog blocks interaction with the rest of the page.

questions.question: In anchor positioning, what does `position-try-fallbacks: flip-block` do?
options: Makes the element a block-level box
Hides the element when the anchor scrolls away
Tries the position mirrored on the block axis (for example above instead of below) if the original placement overflows
Creates a new anchor name for the element
questions.explanation: Fallbacks are tried in order when the element would overflow its containing block. flip-block mirrors the placement across the block axis. Hiding on scroll is position-visibility.
